slides.title: Claude Pricing Starting June 15, 2026 , Anthropic
slides.text: Claude Pricing Starting June 15, 2026 , Anthropic splits Claude into two separate usage buckets If you have a Pro or Max subscription, its limits stay the same and covers interactive use - but only when you are using Anthropic tools: Claude Code in the terminal, Cowork, and chat Pro: ~44K tokens per 5-hour window Max 5x ($100) = 5x Pro (up to 220K tokens per 5-hour window) Max 20x ($200) = 20x Pro (up to 880K tokens per 5-hour window) Additionally paid subscribers will get a new, separate monthly Agent SDK credit (at standard API token costs) to cover "automated" use - Agent SDK calls , claude -p, GitHub Actions, and third-party apps The dollar size of the credit is the same as subscription ($20, $100, $200). Credits don't roll over. Once depleted, SDK calls stop. You have an option to enable "extra usage" at standard API costs Ultracode = xhigh reasoning effort  + Dynamic Workflows (span many subagents) /effort ultracode Both Pro and Max subscribers can use it Max has Dynamic Workflows "ON" by default It requires Opus 4.8 or 4.7 and won't appear on Sonnet 4.6 After June 15th, terminal sessions (Claude Code CLI) remain unaffected, but headless use via "claude -p" draws from the new Agent SDK credit Beware: ultracode carries no spending cap and can exhaust your session budget extremely quickly. Claude Ultracode = xhigh reasoning + Dynamic Workflows Starting June 22, 2026 Claude Fable 5 will be removed from monthly subscriptions. It iwll be only available via credits at API token pricing.

slides.text: AI Updates Eli Lilly and Company ( https://www.lilly.com/ ) founded in 1876 by Colonel Eli Lilly in Indianapolis, Indiana A 150-year-old pharmaceutical giant employing over 50K people with a ~$1 Trillion market cap Known for GLP-1 blockbusters Mounjaro and Zepbound, Lilly is rapidly repositioning as an AI-powered drug discovery platform Its TuneLab initiative (tunelab.lilly.com) gives biotech startups access to AI/ML models trained on Lilly's vast proprietary research Key partnerships include Nvidia (1,000 Blackwell GPUs), Google DeepMind's Isomorphic Labs (AlphaFold), and a $2.8B deal with Insilico Medicine Its core moat: 150 years of irreplaceable proprietary metabolic disease data covering diabetes and obesity that no public-data-trained AI model can replicate.

slides.title: How to make a harness Harness Engineering -
slides.text: How to make a harness Harness Engineering - by Mehdi Allahyari Harness - execution environment, safety rails, and feedback loops around an LLM Reliable agents come not from bigger models but from better infrastructure LLM = car engine, Harness = chassis, brakes, and steering A harness typically provides an execution loop, context compaction, a secure sandbox, lifecycle hooks, and human-in-the-loop gates Feedforward controls (configs), feedback controls (self-correction) Tuning the harness beats upgrading the model https://substack.com/home/post/p-200045389 Five architectural pillars: a State Controller maintaining durable conversation history a Tool Registry validating and dispatching tool calls an Execution Sandbox isolating commands Middleware hooks intercepting calls before and after execution Boundary Controls enforcing hard limits like iteration caps Example - in python using Anthropic API Errors become structured feedback rather than crashes, letting the model self-correct while guaranteed termination keeps the system safe to run unsupervised https://mlnotes.substack.com/p/inside-the-machine-the-anatomy-of Part 3 will cover sandboxing and execution security.

slides.title: Fraud Detection - and AI Most fraud detection
slides.text: Fraud Detection - and AI Most fraud detection today runs on classical ML - Isolation Forest, XGBoost - plus good feature engineering and rules Deep Learning or LLMs have narrow use cases - documents, images - and adversarial LLM-generated attacks Rules - deterministic, hand-written logic Velocity checks - block if >N transactions in T minutes Amount thresholds - flag big transactions Geo-blocking - deny from specific countries or IPs Blacklists - match against known bad accts, cards, devices Time-of-day rules - flag outside normal business hours Card-not-present rules - apply stricter checks for online vs. in-person Modern AI - LLM/deep learning LLM-based document analysis — understanding free-text insurance claims, loan applications, or support tickets for deceptive language; requires semantic understanding, not just features Multimodal forgery detection - combining vision + language models to detect forged IDs, manipulated invoices, or deepfake KYC (Know Your Customer) videos LLM-generated attack detection - defending against AI-written phishing emails or synthetic identity narratives requires a model that understands language at the same level the attacker used Conversational fraud probing - an LLM agent asks follow-up questions during onboarding and detects inconsistencies in answers Classical / Adaptive ML Isolation Forest, Random Cut Forest (AWS), One-Class SVM, Classifiers - Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, etc, Clustering (K-Means / DBSCAN), Autoencoders (high reconstruction error = likely fraud ), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs / LSTMs) - detect unusual temporal patterns; Graph algorithms (PageRank, Louvain) - detect fraud rings and money laundering networks from account relationship graphs

slides.title: AI Updates Stateful Swarms: How Persistent Memory Beats
slides.text: AI Updates Stateful Swarms: How Persistent Memory Beats Traditional Agent Architectures https://www.artificialintelligencemadesimple.com/p/stateful-swarms-how-persistent-memory Stateful Swarms is an agentic architecture that replaces long-context prompts and stateless multi-agent chains with a persistent “blackboard” memory shared by specialized workers Agents read from and write to an append-only, typed knowledge base with provenance, so documents are read once and then queried cheaply and repeatedly instead of being reprocessed each run On the 1,251-task Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark, this design achieved 17.75% strict all-pass at about $1.30 per task, versus Harvey’s 10.4% at roughly $50.90, yielding about 39x cost reduction using the same Gemini models The paper argues that persistent state, auditability, and structured coordination matter more than raw model scale for scalable knowledge work Agent Arena https://arena.ai/leaderboard/agent - live, crowdsourced leaderboard ranking AI models on real-world agentic tool use across 455K+ sessions, currently led by Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT 5.5 https:// docs.factory.ai/benchmarks/agent-arena - uses Elo-based crowdsourced voting to compare coding agents on complex autonomous tasks https:// microsoft.github.io/WindowsAgentArena - benchmarks multimodal desktop agents on 150+ Windows OS tasks, with the best agent reaching only 19.5% vs. 74.5% human success https:// arena.xlang.ai - XLang Lab's Computer Agent Arena - open platform for evaluating computer-use agents on real desktop tasks across Windows and Ubuntu

slides.title: AI in Snowflake Snowflake Cortex - use LLMs
slides.text: AI in Snowflake Snowflake Cortex - use LLMs and ML models inside Snowflake https://docs.snowflake.com/en/guides-overview-ai-features https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/features/cortex/ https://www.snowflake.com/en/product/ai/ https://www.snowflake.com/en/blog/integrated-developer-environment-ai/ AISQL - Cortex AI Functions - call LLMs directly from SQL to summarize, classify, translate, or extract from text, images, and audio Cortex Analyst - natural language to SQL conversion Cortex Agents - multi-step reasoning across structured and unstructured data Cortex Search - RAG-style semantic search over your Snowflake data Cortex Fine-tuning - fine-tune select models on your own data Snowflake CoCo (formerly Cortex Code) - AI coding agent within Snowsight Snowflake CoWork - a personal work agent - query data, run deep research, and act in Slack, Gmail, Jira, and Salesforce Snowflake Cortex can use various LLMs - Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake's own Arctic LLM, and various task-specific models for translation, summarization, sentiment analysis, and document processing Managed MCP servers - making Snowflake a data backend for your own agents Snowflake Cortex Code CLI - with MCP and ACP (Agent Client Protocol) support Snowflake ML - traditional ML models (forecasting, classification, etc.) using a feature store, model registry, and framework connectors for popular libraries AI runs inside Snowflake's governance perimeter . Your data is never used to train shared models and is not accessible to other customers. Standard RBAC, data masking, and row-level policies apply to AI features just like regular data access Snowflake has 9K employees and current valuation is ~ 82-88 Bln

slides.title: Databricks at $165B Valuation Databricks in talks for
slides.text: Databricks at $165B  Valuation Databricks in talks for funding at $165 billion valuation Databricks was founded in 2013 by seven researchers from UC Berkeley's AMPLab, the same team that created Apache Spark in 2009 to fix Hadoop MapReduce's slowness Apache Spark has introduced in-memory distributed computing with high-level APIs in Scala and Python, making big data processing dramatically faster and more accessible Databricks commercialized Spark by offering managed clusters, collaborative notebooks, and a unified platform for batch and streaming workloads using distributed DataFrames as the core abstraction In 2019, Databricks introduced Delta Lake - an open-source storage layer built on top of Parquet files that adds ACID transactions , versioning, and reliable metadata handling to data lakes This "lakehouse" architecture merges the flexibility of data lakes with the reliability of data warehouses Today, Databricks has expanded deeply into AI: it hosts MLflow for experiment tracking, supports LLM fine-tuning, integrates models from OpenAI and Anthropic, and recently launched Agent Bricks for production-scale AI agent development https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Databricks - 10K employees https://www.databricks.com Databricks has robust SQL support Databricks has a multi-layer security model with full RBAC and fine-grained data visibility controls (RBAC - Role-Based Access Control - GRANT / REVOKE SQL statements on catalogs, schemas, and tables; Row-level security (RLS) — filter rows based on the querying user's identity; Column-level security — mask or restrict access to specific columns; ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) — dynamic policies based on user attributes, currently in private preview; Audit logs and data lineage — track who queried what and when). Snowflake vs Databricks Pick Snowflake if you mostly doing SQL and run BI dashboards and reports from structured or semi-structured data Pick Databricks if you need serious ML, LLM fine-tuning, or AI agent pipelines; if you work with streaming data or mixed data types (logs, unstructured text, etc.); if you want open formats (no lock-in) and multi-language flexibility with Python/Scala; when you do complex data transformations at scale

slides.title: Samwer Brothers Copy-Cats Samwer brothers - Multi-Billion Copy-cats
slides.text: Samwer Brothers Copy-Cats Samwer brothers - Multi-Billion Copy-cats 3 brothers from Germany - have built a Multi-Billion Empire using the following copy-cat strategy: Find a hot U.S. startup, Copy it fast, Launch it in Europe, Sell it to the original company In 1999 - cloned eBay as Alando, sold to eBay just 100 days later for $43M In 2004 they built Jamba!, a mobile content platform, sold to Verisign for $273M In 2007, they founded Rocket Internet to do this cloning massively, for example: CityDeal - sold to Groupon Zalando (IPO valued at €5.3B) Lazada Jumia Foodpanda ... and dozens more across over 50 countries Rocket Internet itself went public in 2014 at a €6.5 Bln valuation Today, each brother is worth over $1 billion https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Internet The Wildest Part - the original companies (like eBay, Groupon, or Airbnb) were grateful, because the Samwer brothers were basically doing their international expansion for them https://stories.byburk.net/how-three-brothers-made-billions-by-shamelessly-copying-ideas-6ab866cd420c

Multiple salary guides report AI/ML engineers earning 10–20% more than general software engineers, especially in US tech hubs Example ranges: entry‑level software engineers often see 85k–105k base in the US, while entry‑level AI engineers commonly start around 100k–120k, with total comp 130k–160k Recent guides put the median US AI engineer base around 130k+, not counting equity and bonuses, reinforcing that AI roles sit at the high end of the SWE spectrum The premium tends to grow with specialization (LLMs, generative models, MLOps, infra/agentic systems) and at companies where AI is core business, but you still see overlap: a top‑tier infra SWE in FAANG‑ish environments can match or exceed many generic "AI engineer" roles.
